steps.what: Locate applicable machinery blueprints and manufacturer manuals for the installed equipment
Study blueprints and manuals to determine correct machinery installation or operation

tasks.design: Configure equipment-linked document retrieval in {OTHER} maintenance management software. The mechanic confirms applicability and reads the relevant original material; retrieval does not generate machinery instructions or resolve technical ambiguity.
tasks.previous_blocker: Applicable manuals can be difficult to find among revisions and variants.
tasks.enabler_now: Native equipment records can link to controlled documents and searchable metadata.
tasks.still_hard: Modified machines and instructions whose applicability is uncertain.
tasks.human_edge: Connecting the installed configuration with the correct technical requirements.
tasks.altitude: Less manual hunting; interpretation and work authority remain unchanged.

reach.task: Resolve a mismatch between installed machinery and available documentation
reach.learn: How configuration changes affect document applicability

evidence.claim: Equipment-linked document search is a plausible native configuration; the digest does not establish this particular deployment or saving.

assumptions: Boundary is locating and studying references, excluding installation, operation and writing new procedures.

The existing asset-registration process produces asset ID, manufacturer, model, serial/configuration and document references; document control provides revision and issue status through unchanged work.
s1 retains machine identity and document-applicability checks, including manual register lookup where metadata is missing; no new tagging labour is assumed for free.
s2 retains reading and technical interpretation. No generated summary substitutes for the relevant source instructions.
Test native asset/document links first; where metadata must be created, measure that capture before claiming this benefit.
unknowns: Asset metadata, controlled-document coverage and retrieval time
research_questions: Does native equipment-linked retrieval reduce hunting after applicability checks?

already_counted.description: Document selection, applicability checks and fallback in s1

incremental.description: Inspect stale asset links and report configuration mismatches

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=10+75=85; gross 15 minus 1 focal upkeep gives net 14. High requires existing reliable metadata and repeated hunting; low covers manual lookup and configuration uncertainty. Document-control upkeep is separate.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Determine required machinery codes and instructions from authorised job and machine requirements
Enter codes and instructions into the computer-controlled machinery interface
Verify entered program under the established machinery checking and release procedure

tasks.design: Retain authorised program selection, entry through {OTHER} machinery-control software and the established verification process. A general code generator is not introduced as a replacement for equipment-specific programming and checks.
tasks.previous_blocker: Correctness depends on machine configuration and physical behaviour, not only syntax.
tasks.enabler_now: No validated reusable program library or supported import contract is established for this task.
tasks.still_hard: Configuration differences and instructions that alter hazardous physical behaviour.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising when the intended program does not fit the actual machinery.
tasks.altitude: No change to machinery programming authority or verification duties.

reach.learn: Which program changes require specialist validation

evidence.claim: The retained workflow makes no claim that general software generation replaces equipment-specific programming checks.

assumptions: Boundary is authorised mechanic programming work; engineering approval and final machine release remain in the existing local process.
s1 produces selected instructions through retained technical assessment; no free structured machine program or safety approval is assumed.
s2 and s3 retain all entry and verification time. This graph is not an operating or testing instruction.
No new system, automatic control write or upkeep is introduced.
unknowns: Controller types, import features and local authority limits
research_questions: Does a validated native program library already exist, and is manual entry a genuine remaining burden?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=35+35+30=100. Program selection, entry and verification retain their time; incremental upkeep is zero.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Demonstrate equipment functions and features to machine operators and answer questions

tasks.design: Keep the actual demonstration and questions with the mechanic. Existing {DOCS} references may support the session, but a generated explanation does not replace showing the installed equipment and checking understanding.
tasks.previous_blocker: The work is practical communication about a particular machine.
tasks.enabler_now: No separate repetitive content-authoring burden has been established.
tasks.still_hard: Adapting explanations to operators and recognising misunderstood behaviour.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing confusion and explaining the equipment in its actual context.
tasks.altitude: No change to equipment demonstration duties.

reach.task: Arrange further support for operators who need more practice

evidence.claim: The direct equipment demonstration remains human work and has no claimed software saving.

assumptions: Boundary is the mechanic's demonstration, excluding operators' productive work and separate training administration.
s1 includes observing understanding and answering questions; no structured competence feed is assumed.
Approved procedures are unchanged upstream references, with no extra authoring transferred to others.
No new system or ongoing upkeep is introduced.
unknowns: Equipment variety and operators' learning needs
research_questions: Is repetitive reference preparation a separately measurable part of this work?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100. Demonstration and questions retain all time with zero new upkeep.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Gather maintenance jobs crew availability skills and access constraints
Prepare draft work crew schedules from checked job and availability constraints
Check crew schedule assign work and discuss changes with crews

tasks.design: Configure an editable crew board in {OTHER} maintenance management software with job, shift and availability fields. Reduce repeated roster entry while the authorised mechanic checks feasibility, assigns the exact schedule and discusses changes; no model ranks individual workers.
tasks.previous_blocker: Crew schedules need repeated copying and adjustment across separate lists.
tasks.enabler_now: Native planning boards can reuse work orders and show explicit conflicts.
tasks.still_hard: Unexpected failures, safe access and whether a crew is suitable for a particular job.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing a practical assignment and hearing crew concerns before work.
tasks.altitude: Less roster maintenance; assignment rights remain within the existing role.

reach.task: Resolve job priorities and access conflicts beyond the mechanic's scope
reach.learn: How shutdown windows constrain feasible schedules

evidence.claim: An editable crew board can reduce schedule administration while retaining assignment judgement; this is a model-knowledge design rather than a measured digest case.

assumptions: Boundary is the mechanic's crew-scheduling task where locally authorised; crew execution and planner decisions remain outside and unchanged.
s1 counts confirmation and capture of job ID, priority, expected duration, required qualification, crew/shift availability and access window; the mechanic produces checked inputs.
Existing work orders and qualification records are upstream references from unchanged planning/HR work, not a complete free scheduling feed.
s2 retains board input, manual sequencing and exceptions. Missing constraints use the current manual planning route.
Test native boards first. s3 retains full feasibility check and crew conversation; any changed job, crew or time requires renewed approval.
Access and employee consultation requirements need local confirmation; no behaviour-based allocation is introduced.
unknowns: Local scheduling authority, native board capability and capture burden
research_questions: Does the board reduce actual roster rewriting after all input confirmation and schedule checking?

already_counted.description: Board input and manual sequencing in s2
Feasibility check, assignment approval and crew discussion in s3

incremental.description: Maintain board settings and investigate stale job/crew entries

approvals.approved_version: Exact job/crew assignments, shifts, dates, access windows and schedule revision; any change voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=35+14+30=79; gross 21 minus 1.5 upkeep gives net 19.5. High requires repeat schedule copying; low covers rapidly changing constraints and manual replanning consuming the benefit.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce reference hunting and roster entry while retaining technical and crew judgement.
reach: Connect equipment context with engineers and maintenance planners
role.ambitious_version: Maintain dependable references and crew plans without weakening machinery accountability.
